title: Songbook and Promise
premise: Noor Fairweather has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's truths while burying her own—specifically the confession she never gave Elias Vance, the winemaker she loved and abandoned in their twenties. Hired to ghostwrite the memoirs of Julian Marsh, Elias's rival vintner, she is trapped by a snowstorm at a remote vineyard where both men are stranded together. As the storm forces the three of them into close quarters, old wounds reopen, Julian discovers her authorship of his rival's celebrated memoirs, and Noor must choose between professional invisibility and the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: that she left because loving him felt like losing herself. She says it before the first harvest comes in, choosing neither man over her work but herself alongside love—and finds belonging not in being chosen, but in finally being seen.
about_author: Hazel Eastwick is the pen name of a former speechwriter who spent years putting words in strangers' mouths before claiming her own. She writes romance about people who are fluent in everyone's language except their own, from a drafty farmhouse she shares with an opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In her Brooklyn apartment, Noor delivers a finished manuscript to a famous client who will take full credit, then accepts a lucrative new contract: the memoirs of Julian Marsh, celebrity vintner. The emotional beat is weary professionalism masking loneliness; she has perfected disappearing into other people's voices.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Reviewing Julian's contract, Noor learns his vineyard borders land owned by Elias Vance—the man whose name she hasn't spoken aloud in ten years. Her agent dismisses her hesitation as superstition. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve: she tells herself a decade is long enough to make anyone a stranger.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Harvest
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At Vale Marsh Vineyard, Julian prepares for harvest and resents the ghostwriter arriving mid-crisis—a rival is undercutting his prices and poaching his distributor. He wants a memoir that will win the war. The beat is ambition laced with insecurity; he needs a story more than he admits.

chapters.title: The Interview Begins
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor arrives at the vineyard and begins interviewing Julian, whose charm is real but whose answers are curated. She recognizes the performance because she writes them. The beat is wary mutual respect—two professionals circling each other's masks.

chapters.title: Snowfall Warning
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Across the valley, Elias preps his own harvest, having just learned Julian hired a ghostwriter to beat him to press. When his truck breaks down near Vale Marsh as the storm front rolls in, he seeks shelter there—and freezes in the doorway at the sight of Noor. The beat is shock curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Three at the Table
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. The storm seals the roads; all three are stranded. Dinner is a minefield of unspoken history, which Julian senses but cannot name. Noor watches the two rivals perform civility. The beat is claustrophobic tension—the past tense refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Sent to catalog Julian's wine library, Noor finds a bottle labeled with a date she knows intimately: the night she left Elias. Elias finds her there. In the cold dark they have it out in whispers—ten years of blame compressed into one argument. The beat is rupture; the wound reopens properly.

chapters.title: The Rival's Version
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian interviews Elias separately, ostensibly about industry history, and pieces together that Noor is the woman from Elias's stories—the one who vanished. His memoir suddenly has a better plot than his own life. The beat is conflicted opportunism turning toward something dangerously like empathy.

chapters.title: Power Out
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. The storm knocks out power. Candles, board games, generator triage force cooperation between enemies. Noor fixes the generator wiring—a skill from her invisible years—and both men see her clearly for the first time. The beat is warmth under pressure; the triangle softens into something human.

chapters.title: Manuscript Leak
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Julian discovers a draft chapter revealing Noor ghostwrote Elias's acclaimed memoir years ago—the secret weapon behind his reputation. Feeling betrayed on both fronts, Julian threatens to expose her and void the contract. The beat is betrayal compounding betrayal; her invisibility weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Justice, Unofficial
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Julian privately—not to defend Noor's secrecy but to name what Julian is really doing: punishing her for a system both industries built. They strike a truce outside any law but their own: settle it at harvest, man to man, no lawyers, no leaks. The beat is grudging honor between rivals.

chapters.title: Rehearsed Lines
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Alone in her room, Noor drafts and destroys a dozen versions of the confession she owes Elias. Flashback threads reveal their twenties: a shared apartment, her fear that his rising star would erase her, the cowardly exit. The beat is excavation—understanding, finally, why she ran.

chapters.title: Blizzard Work
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Unable to sleep, Julian reads Noor's discarded drafts and realizes her voice is the best thing he's ever been handed—and that publishing it under his name alone would be theft. He begins rewriting the contract in his head. The beat is conscience catching up with ambition.

chapters.title: Thaw Negotiations
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Roads partially clear; the storm's end forces decisions none of them are ready for. Julian offers Noor co-authorship if she stays through harvest; Elias asks nothing except the truth. Noor defers both, buying time. The beat is the eye of the storm—calm that feels like avoidance.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Working the vines side by side with Elias, Noor almost says the sentence and fails again. Instead she tells him a smaller truth—that she's been ghostwriting so long she no longer knows her own voice. He answers that he never forgot hers. The beat is intimacy without resolution; the almost.

chapters.title: The Distributor's Gambit
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian's rival exploits the storm delays, threatening both vineyards' survival. Julian and Elias must jointly court a distributor, forcing public cooperation. Noor drafts the pitch that saves them both. The beat is alliance forged by necessity; rivalry transmuted into reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: Night Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. On the eve of first harvest, the three share a quiet dinner that feels, impossibly, like friendship. Julian announces he'll credit his ghostwriter publicly—whatever she decides. Elias walks Noor to her room and waits, saying nothing, giving her the space to speak or not. The beat is suspended grace.

chapters.title: First Pick
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Harvest begins at dawn; hands in the grapes, laughter, exhaustion. Mid-row, Elias stops her and asks plainly: was any of it real? Noor's rehearsed sentence finally arrives—but she says it new, unrehearsed: she left because she was afraid love meant vanishing, and she's done vanishing. The beat is climax; the decade-long debt paid.

chapters.title: Crush
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian witnesses the reunion and grieves briefly, then chooses integrity: he revises his memoir to tell the true story—including Noor's authorship of the book that shaped him—as a co-written work. The beat is magnanimity earned through loss; the rival becomes an ally.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor signs her first book under her own name in ten years. Elias reads the acknowledgment page standing in the cellar. They negotiate a future slowly—no grand gestures, just terms, like people who've learned what silence costs. The beat is tender pragmatism; love rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: Bottling Day
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The joint bottling of both vineyards' first post-storm vintage. Julian proposes the three collaborate on a wine-book project; Noor accepts as herself, not a ghost. Old grievances get a ceremonial burial—one bottle from the night she left, opened and finally drunk. The beat is reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Songbook and Promise
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A year later, at the launch of the co-authored book, Noor reads aloud in her own voice to a room containing both men, now friends. Elias gives her a songbook of the years apart, last page blank—room to write forward. The beat is belonging achieved: memory honored, justice kept outside the law, love in present tense at last.
